jobs.title: Senior Perception Engineer, Obstacle Foundation Models - Autonomous Vehicles
jobs.description:
Intelligent machines powered by artificial intelligence—computers that can learn, reason, and interact with people—are redefining every industry. GPU-accelerated deep learning provides the foundation for machines to perceive, reason, and solve complex problems. NVIDIA GPUs run deep learning algorithms that simulate aspects of human intelligence, acting as the brain of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can perceive and understand the world.

We are seeking an exceptional Senior Perception Engineer to help design and productize NVIDIA’s next-generation autonomous driving perception stack. You will work on the core 3D obstacle perception pipeline, give to architecture and algorithm design, and remain deeply hands-on with implementation, including modern transformer-based, multi-modal, and vision-language techniques where they add real value.

What You’ll Be Doing

Develop and improve the technical design, architecture, and roadmap for 3D obstacle perception to support end-to-end autonomous driving functionalities, employing innovative CNN and transformer-based architectures where appropriate.
Design and implement advanced 3D perception models using multi-camera inputs and/or multi-sensor fusion (camera, radar, lidar) for obstacle detection and tracking, including opportunities to explore BEV and transformer-based 3D perception.
Build efficient, production-grade deep learning models: define objectives with the team, select and prototype architectures, run experiments, and follow standard methodologies for training and evaluation, using techniques such as large-scale pretraining, distillation, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA).
Help define and maintain critical metric frameworks to quantify perception performance; analyze large-scale real and synthetic datasets to identify failure modes and systematically improve accuracy, robustness, and efficiency, incorporating approaches like self-supervised and representation learning when beneficial.
Contribute to the data strategy for perception: specify data and labeling requirements, help prioritize data collection and annotation, and collaborate with data and ground-truth teams, including model-assisted workflows (e.g., active learning, auto-labeling, vision-language models (VLMs)) and model-in-the-loop tooling.
Collaborate with safety, systems, and software teams to ensure perception solutions meet product requirements for safety, latency, resource usage, and software robustness, and are ready for deployment at scale.

What We Need To See

PhD with 4+ years, MS with 6+ years, or BS (or equivalent experience) with 8+ years of relevant experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
Hands-on experience developing deep learning–based perception or closely related systems for complex real-world problems, with strong proficiency in frameworks such as PyTorch and a track record of taking models from prototype to production.
Validated experience in data-driven development, including close collaboration with data, labeling, and ground-truth teams on data strategy, labeling quality, and iterative model improvement.
Strong programming skills in Python and/or C++, with experience building reliable, high-performance, production-quality software.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience designing and deploying perception solutions for autonomous driving or robotics using camera-based deep learning at scale.
Hands-on experience architecting and deploying DNN-based perception pipelines on embedded or real-time platforms, including optimization for latency, memory, and compute constraints, and experience with modern architectures such as CNNs and transformers, plus familiarity with techniques like large-scale pretraining, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA), or vision-language models (VLMs).
Strong publication record or recognized contributions in deep learning, computer vision, or autonomous systems at leading conferences/journals (e.g., CVPR, ICCV, NeurIPS, IROS).
Deep understanding of 3D computer vision fundamentals, including camera modeling and calibration (intrinsic and extrinsic), multi-view geometry, and 3D representations, ideally with experience applying these concepts in transformer-based 3D or BEV perception pipelines.
Experience with CUDA development and optimizing training or inference pipelines through custom CUDA kernels or other GPU-accelerated components.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation
jobs.description:
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what's never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world's best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you'll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world.

We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our new User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation team. You will own the systems our research runs on: the architecture, scale, and releases of our open-source framework. You'll also build the environments where simulated users meet models and agents. User simulation is quickly becoming core infrastructure for evaluating and training AI models and agents. They are judged by how they work with users, people or other agents, over many turns: holding a conversation, using tools, or collaborating on code in a real repository. Real data is thinnest here: slow and costly to collect, skewed toward existing users, and missing the long tail of languages, domains, and safety scenarios. We build grounded synthetic users and simulators, then use both to find capability gaps and close them with targeted training data and RL environments. A lot of our work ships as open source, including NeMo User Sim, Nemotron-Personas, and the data and environments we generate. We build our own systems on these same tools. We publish and present at top conferences, and we organize UserSim @ NeurIPS 2026, the first NeurIPS workshop on user simulation. The team serves three groups:

Internal partners, including Nemotron and other model, agent, and product teams who evaluate and train their models with our simulators.
Open-source users and contributors who build on the framework for their own models, agents, and languages.
The research community, through work that pushes the state of the art and is published at top venues.

The mission is the boss. We organize around the problem, not titles or ownership. Researchers write production code, engineers shape research, and everyone works directly with partner teams. We share credit, review each other's work candidly, and pick up whatever moves the mission forward.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the architecture of NeMo User Sim: the conversation engine, configuration-driven pipelines, and extension API.
Scale simulation to tens of thousands of concurrent multi-turn episodes against hosted and self-served models (e.g., vLLM, NIM), sharded across Slurm or Kubernetes. Runs must survive rate limits and partial failures, resume cleanly, and reproduce down to the row.
Build and run environments for agents. These include stateful simulated tool services, and sandboxed coding environments where simulated users work with coding agents on real repositories. Verifiers and hidden tests grade the results.
Connect simulated users to NeMo Gym and RL training, and keep the loop fast and cheap.
Turn research prototypes into reliable, tested features together with research scientists.
Run the open-source project: versioned releases, CI/CD, dependency and license hygiene, issue triage, and contributor reviews. Build the pipelines behind our open data releases, onboard internal partner teams, and present the framework at conferences.

What We Need To See

BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
6+ years building production ML systems, data pipelines, or developer libraries.
Expert Python skills, with a track record of typed, tested libraries that other teams depend on.
Experience running LLM workloads at scale: serving (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NIM), concurrency, and cost.
Experience with LLM evaluation, training-data pipelines, or agents that use tools.
Strong software design judgment on interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility, with the mission ahead of ownership and credit.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Maintaining a widely used open-source ML library.
RL training infrastructure or environments, such as NeMo Gym or NeMo RL.
Infrastructure for coding agents: container sandboxes and SWE-bench-style harnesses.
Inference optimization: distillation, quantization, or speculative decoding.
Experience with NeMo Data Designer, Ray, or Spark and experience with multilingual text processing, such as language identification, scripts, and localization.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world's most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, and you want to build the open-source infrastructure behind trustworthy user simulation, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:

187,500 USD – 364,000 USD for Level 4; and 232,500 USD – 442,000 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

jobs.title: Senior ML Applied Scientist , Frontier AI Startup Team
jobs.description:
Description

AI-native startups now train their own models, post-train open-weight models for their products, and serve inference at volumes where cost per output decides their margins. The startup team of the AWS Frontier AI Services puts applied scientists to work directly with those founders and their engineers. We're hiring a Senior Applied Scientist in North America to own those engagements with our strategists end to end: scope the problem with the founding team, design and run the experiments, and ship working code into the startup's stack on AWS. The problems are open-ended and the timelines run in weeks, so your scientific judgment sets both the approach and the bar for done.

Key job responsibilities

Work directly with founders, CTOs and ML leads at AI startups to define the problem and agree on a production target and an evaluation plan. Then deliver against them in six-to-twelve-week engagements, with the startup's own engineers working alongside you.
Improve model quality for the startup's use case by post-training open-weight models. That covers supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning (for example GRPO), distillation, and the synthetic data and evaluation sets that show whether it worked.
Cut training and inference cost and latency on NVIDIA GPUs and AWS Trainium. Profile where the compute goes, apply quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, batching, parallelism and kernel-level tuning, and measure cost per output before and after.
Invent new methods when published ones fall short of the customer's target, and publish the results at peer-reviewed venues, on AWS blogs and as open-source code.
Turn each engagement into assets the next one can reuse: reference implementations, evaluation harnesses and playbooks. Take the gaps you find in Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker and AWS Trainium back to those service teams as specific requests.
Raise the science bar on the team. Review experiment designs and code, mentor scientists and engineers, and help account teams and strategists judge which startup requests need a scientist.

A day in the life

You start the day on a call with the CTO of a robotics startup whose vision-language model misses objects in low light. Before anyone changes the model, you agree on an evaluation set built from their own camera footage. Mid-morning you check an overnight reinforcement-learning run for another startup: reward is up but two task categories regressed, so you write up why and what to try next. After lunch you join an AWS account manager and a GenAI strategist to scope a request from a voice AI company that needs lower inference latency before it scales up. You leave with a two-week profiling plan and one go/no-go metric. You end the day reviewing a teammate's experiment design and editing a workshop paper drawn from last quarter's engagement.

About The Team

We're applied scientists and GenAI strategists working as one team with venture-backed, AI-native startups, from the first discovery call to a model running in production. The work spans large language and vision-language models, agents, voice, multimodal retrieval and physical AI, including world and action models. We judge an engagement by what the startup ships. Startups make platform decisions in weeks, so we scope quickly, share results early, and say plainly when something isn't working. This role focuses on startups in North America. You'll work with AWS account teams, solutions architects and service teams, and with Amazon's wider science community.

Basic Qualifications

PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc.
Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.
6+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience

NVIDIA is seeking a world-class researcher to advance agentic AI for 3D and robotics on the Cosmos team. You will develop AI agents that write and execute code, build and manipulate 3D environments, and solve robotics tasks through simulation and interaction.

A central focus of this role is recursive self-improvement: developing agents that can evaluate their own work, learn from failures, and improve their code, tools, and problem-solving strategies. You will investigate how generative models, coding agents, and simulation can work together to accelerate this process, with rigorous evaluation of capability gains and generalization. You will work with a team of researchers to turn new ideas into research prototypes, scale promising approaches with large datasets and compute, and collaborate with product teams to bring your research into real-world applications.

What You’ll Be Doing

Conduct original research in agentic coding for 3D content creation, simulation, and robotics.
Develop agents that generate, execute, debug, and refine code to construct 3D worlds, build simulation workflows, and solve robotics tasks.
Design recursive self-improvement methods that enable agents to improve their implementations, tools, and strategies through experimentation, execution feedback, and experience.
Build training and evaluation pipelines using simulated environments, synthetic data, and automated task generation.
Develop benchmarks and controlled experiments to measure task success, reliability, generalization, and sustained improvement across iterations.
Collaborate with researchers and product teams to scale successful methods and transfer research into products.
Communicate research findings through publications, prototypes, and technical demonstrations.

What We Need To See

Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
5+ years of relevant research experience.
A track record of research excellence or significant technical contributions to deployed systems.
Strong knowledge of deep learning, with expertise in one or more of the following: coding agents, reinforcement learning, program synthesis, generative models, computer graphics, 3D vision, or robotics.
Experience building systems that connect models with executable tools, environments, or simulators.
Excellent Python programming skills, proficiency in C++, and experience with modern deep learning frameworks.
Experience training and evaluating large-scale models and building or curating datasets.
Excellent collaboration, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Research on self-improving agents, automated discovery, code generation, or learning from execution feedback.
Experience with 3D simulation, procedural environment generation, robot learning, or embodied AI.
Experience designing evaluations that distinguish robust capability improvements from benchmark overfitting.
Demonstrated ability to build end-to-end research systems that combine model training, tool use, simulation, and evaluation.

195,000 USD – 370,500 USD for Level 4; and 232,500 USD – 448,500 USD for Level 5.

jobs.title: Senior ML Applied Scientist , Frontier AI Startup Team
jobs.description:
Description

AI-native startups now train their own models, post-train open-weight models for their products, and serve inference at volumes where cost per output decides their margins. The startup team of the AWS Frontier AI Services puts applied scientists to work directly with those founders and their engineers. We're hiring a Senior Applied Scientist in North America to own those engagements with our strategists end to end: scope the problem with the founding team, design and run the experiments, and ship working code into the startup's stack on AWS. The problems are open-ended and the timelines run in weeks, so your scientific judgment sets both the approach and the bar for done.

Key job responsibilities

Work directly with founders, CTOs and ML leads at AI startups to define the problem and agree on a production target and an evaluation plan. Then deliver against them in six-to-twelve-week engagements, with the startup's own engineers working alongside you.
Improve model quality for the startup's use case by post-training open-weight models. That covers supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning (for example GRPO), distillation, and the synthetic data and evaluation sets that show whether it worked.
Cut training and inference cost and latency on NVIDIA GPUs and AWS Trainium. Profile where the compute goes, apply quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, batching, parallelism and kernel-level tuning, and measure cost per output before and after.
Invent new methods when published ones fall short of the customer's target, and publish the results at peer-reviewed venues, on AWS blogs and as open-source code.
Turn each engagement into assets the next one can reuse: reference implementations, evaluation harnesses and playbooks. Take the gaps you find in Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker and AWS Trainium back to those service teams as specific requests.
Raise the science bar on the team. Review experiment designs and code, mentor scientists and engineers, and help account teams and strategists judge which startup requests need a scientist.

A day in the life

You start the day on a call with the CTO of a robotics startup whose vision-language model misses objects in low light. Before anyone changes the model, you agree on an evaluation set built from their own camera footage. Mid-morning you check an overnight reinforcement-learning run for another startup: reward is up but two task categories regressed, so you write up why and what to try next. After lunch you join an AWS account manager and a GenAI strategist to scope a request from a voice AI company that needs lower inference latency before it scales up. You leave with a two-week profiling plan and one go/no-go metric. You end the day reviewing a teammate's experiment design and editing a workshop paper drawn from last quarter's engagement.

About The Team

We're applied scientists and GenAI strategists working as one team with venture-backed, AI-native startups, from the first discovery call to a model running in production. The work spans large language and vision-language models, agents, voice, multimodal retrieval and physical AI, including world and action models. We judge an engagement by what the startup ships. Startups make platform decisions in weeks, so we scope quickly, share results early, and say plainly when something isn't working. This role focuses on startups in North America. You'll work with AWS account teams, solutions architects and service teams, and with Amazon's wider science community.

Basic Qualifications

PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc.
Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.
6+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience

The role

This is a hybrid role: a designer who builds, or an engineer who designs. You have the eye to know what good looks like and the code to make it repeatable. You build and run the automated workstreams that Fanatics Casino, and the teams around it, produce brand-safe creative from every day: template and variant generators, image and video generation with our rules built in, copy-to-layout pipelines, Figma plugins.

The stack is already here: a shared Figma design system, Figma Motion and Figma Buzz for locked self-serve templates, Figma Weave for generative image and video, Creative Engine for automated static and video assets, and Runway. You turn them into automated templates and workflows that CRM, performance marketing and partners run themselves, with brand, responsible gaming and compliance rules built in so the output is right by default; you own best-in-class video generation, and train the models that keep generated imagery and video looking like us. The tools you make are run by CRM managers, performance marketers and designers across in-app, CRM and paid. You can build, not just brief. Design judgement decides what gets built.

What You’ll Do

Build and execute automated workstreams for teams including CRM, performance marketing, partners and design: template and variant generators, copy-to-layout pipelines, Figma plugins and automation scripts that go from brief to approved asset, connecting the existing stack end to end (design system components into Buzz templates, Weave agent workflows for promo imagery, Creative Engine extended from Markets into CRM and in-app).
Own best-in-class video generation: set up and run the generative video pipeline across Weave, Runway and Creative Engine for hooks, variants, start frames and localisations, and decide which tool does what where they overlap.
Train and maintain LoRAs and custom models on the Casino visual identity, products, characters and partner assets so generated imagery and video stay on-brand without hand-fixing; retrain when the brand or a partner changes.
Encode the Casino visual identity, responsible gaming requirements and market-specific compliance rules into every workstream, so a CRM manager or performance marketer can run it and the output is safe by default: disclaimer and RG messaging legible and correctly placed at every size. Creative approves anything new.
Target the highest-volume executions first (CRM banners, in-app promo cards, paid variants) and measure the before and after in hours per asset.

Comfort in a regulated category where some outputs must never ship, and the instinct to design for that.
Clear communication with non-technical colleagues, and the patience to train the people who will run what you build.

Dynamic creative or creative automation platforms (Celtra, Storyteq, Bannerflow, Creatopy) and a view on where they fall short.

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Solutions Architecture (SA) organization helps Stripe's most strategic customers design and validate technical solutions that drive their business forward. Within SA, our team builds the tools, workflows, and custom technical assets that make the broader SA org more effective—turning individual ingenuity into org-wide capability.

We are looking for AI Engineers who are energized by working close to the business and the users we serve. You'll operate as an embedded, high-context engineer focused on the highest-leverage opportunities across the SA org—building production-quality tooling, supporting our most strategic engagements, and shipping automation that meaningfully improves how Solutions Architects work every day.

What You'll Do

As an AI Engineer, you'll be embedded directly with the Solutions Architecture team—building alongside them, deeply understanding their workflows, and shipping tools and automation that permanently change how they operate. Your measure of success is SA productivity: the engagements you've accelerated, the workflows you've transformed, and the tools you've built that the org adopts as default.

You'll ship code daily. You'll discover where SAs lose time and build high-impact solutions. You'll take what works for one person and scale it to work for the org. And when our most strategic customer engagements need custom technical assets, you'll build those too.

This is a role for someone who wants to work at the intersection of engineering and business impact—close to customers, close to revenue, and building for people you can see using your work every day.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with Solutions Architects, SA leadership, Product, and Engineering to scope technical work and translate ambiguous business needs into well-defined deliverables
Evaluate and integrate AI capabilities (LLMs, agents, workflow automation) where they provide genuine leverage—not for novelty, but for measurable productivity improvement
Architect and build internal tools, agents, and automated workflows that accelerate SA and manager productivity across technical discovery, solution design, demoing, user engagements, territory/pipeline management, and product interlock
Take high-potential tools and workflows built by SAs and managers and harden them into scalable, maintainable, production-grade solutions
Identify patterns across SA workflows and proactively build solutions that address recurring friction
Build custom demo environments, PoC applications, and technical assets for Stripe's most strategic customer engagements
Document tools, architectures, and usage patterns so others can adopt and extend what you've built
Debug, extend, and maintain backend systems across a variety of codebases and infrastructure

Minimum Requirements

4+ years of experience as an engineer shipping production systems
Strong backend engineering fundamentals: you can debug a failing system, trace issues across services, and reason about data flows
Experience building and deploying AI agents, LLM-powered tools, or workflow automation beyond basic prompt engineering
Experience scoping and delivering work with minimal oversight in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment
Proficiency in at least two of: Ruby, Node.js, Python, or Next.js
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) including deployment, monitoring, and basic DevOps
Experience building internal tools, developer platforms, or workflow automation
Demonstrated ability to work across multiple codebases and technology stacks simultaneously
Hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools in your engineering workflow—you're fluent with AI-assisted development but not dependent on it; you can reason through problems and debug without AI as a crutch
Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can translate technical decisions for non-technical stakeholders and navigate cross-functional collaboration naturally
Comfort with ambiguity—you can take a loosely-defined business problem, scope the engineering work, and ship iteratively without waiting for a perfect spec

Preferred Qualifications

Experience designing systems that non-engineers can build on top of or extend themselves (e.g., platforms, low-code frameworks, template systems)
Experience in a Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or GTM Engineering role—or a product engineering role where you worked closely with customers or go-to-market teams
Familiarity with Stripe's products, APIs, or the payments/fintech domain
Experience integrating with third-party platforms (Salesforce, Gong, etc.)
Track record of building tools or systems that were adopted beyond your immediate team
Background in consulting, professional services, or other roles that blend technical depth with business context

Who You Are

Beyond the technical requirements, we're looking for a specific kind of engineer:

You want to be close to the business. You're energized by seeing your work directly impact how a sales team wins a deal or how a customer succeeds.
You're a pragmatic builder. You ship working solutions quickly, iterate based on real usage, and know when "good enough now" beats "perfect later." You'd rather show a working prototype today than present a roadmap deck next quarter.
You're a software engineer by practice. You can architect systems, debug production issues, write clean code, and reason about tradeoffs. AI is a tool in your belt, not a substitute for engineering judgment.
You're a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it generalizes. You think in reusable systems, not one-off scripts.
You thrive without a traditional product team structure. No PRDs landing in your lap, no dedicated PM, no sprint ceremonies. You identify the highest-leverage problem, scope the work, and ship it. You're comfortable trading on-call rotations and rigid processes for autonomy and impact.
You're a strong communicator. You can partner with SAs who are domain experts, understand their workflows deeply enough to build great tools, and explain your technical choices to leadership.

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Stripes on the Works in Progress team based in the London, UK office also work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $172,600 - $258,800. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

, you are supported to do your best work and make a meaningful impact every day. You will be part of a collaborative, physician-led team that works as one and puts patients at the center of everything we do.

With a connected network of providers, care teams, and services across primary and specialty care, surgery centers, imaging, lab, and therapy, you are part of a system designed to deliver high-quality, coordinated care. Together, we create an environment where you can grow, contribute, and help improve the experience and outcomes for every patient we serve.

Benefits

Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits that include healthcare navigation assistance.
Access to a mental health benefit at no cost.
Employer provided life and disability insurance.
$5,250 Tuition Reimbursement per year.
Immediate 401(k) match.
40 hours paid volunteer time off.
A culture committed to community engagement and social impact.

Primary Purpose

The AI Engineer I is an early-career role within the Data & Analytics team, working with the AI/ML team to implement, deploy, and support the AI platforms and models that improve patient care, operations, and the colleague experience. This role is a strong fit for someone with solid programming and cloud fundamentals who wants to grow into AI engineering and MLOps in a healthcare setting. Major Responsibilities

AI platform implementation and integration (40%)

Help configure, build, and integrate conversational AI and virtual assistant solutions on the Kore.ai platform
Support the implementation of Claude-powered applications, including API integrations, prompt and system configuration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, and tool or agent workflows
Integrate AI solutions with enterprise systems, data sources, and APIs in collaboration with data engineers and application teams
Support testing of AI solutions, including functional testing, regression testing, and evaluation of output quality, accuracy, and safety
Document solution designs, configurations, integrations, and release notes

Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code for the deployment of models, prompts, and AI applications across environments
Monitor the performance, availability, usage, latency, and cost of AI solutions, and respond to alerts and incidents
Provide day-to-day support and troubleshooting for AI platforms and the users who depend on them, escalating to vendors and senior engineers as needed

Partner with data scientists, data engineers, architects, application teams, and business stakeholders to define requirements and deliver reliable AI solutions
Communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences, including clinical and operational leaders

Stay current with advances in generative AI, conversational AI, and MLOps practices and share learnings with the team

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in computer science, data science, information systems, engineering, or a related field; or 2 years of related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience
0-2 years of experience in software development, data engineering, DevOps, or machine learning (internships, co-ops, research, and academic projects count)
Proficiency in Python and working knowledge of SQL
Experience working with REST APIs and JSON
Experience with LLMs, prompt engineering, or GenAI frameworks beneficial
Experience with conversational AI or chatbot platforms, such as Kore.ai, beneficial
Experience with Git, CI/CD, and cloud platforms (Azure preferred), Databricks, or MLflow beneficial
Healthcare or Epic experience not required; training provided

Solid foundation in software engineering practices, including version control, testing, and code review
Understanding of how LLMs work, including their strengths and limitations

with the actual pay determined by factors such as skills, experience, education, certifications, geographic location, and internal equity. Additional compensation may be available through shift differentials, bonuses, and other incentives. Base pay is only a portion of the total rewards package.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation
jobs.description:
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what's never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world's best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you'll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world.

We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our new User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation team. You will own the systems our research runs on: the architecture, scale, and releases of our open-source framework. You'll also build the environments where simulated users meet models and agents. User simulation is quickly becoming core infrastructure for evaluating and training AI models and agents. They are judged by how they work with users, people or other agents, over many turns: holding a conversation, using tools, or collaborating on code in a real repository. Real data is thinnest here: slow and costly to collect, skewed toward existing users, and missing the long tail of languages, domains, and safety scenarios. We build grounded synthetic users and simulators, then use both to find capability gaps and close them with targeted training data and RL environments. A lot of our work ships as open source, including NeMo User Sim, Nemotron-Personas, and the data and environments we generate. We build our own systems on these same tools. We publish and present at top conferences, and we organize UserSim @ NeurIPS 2026, the first NeurIPS workshop on user simulation. The team serves three groups:

Internal partners, including Nemotron and other model, agent, and product teams who evaluate and train their models with our simulators.
Open-source users and contributors who build on the framework for their own models, agents, and languages.
The research community, through work that pushes the state of the art and is published at top venues.

The mission is the boss. We organize around the problem, not titles or ownership. Researchers write production code, engineers shape research, and everyone works directly with partner teams. We share credit, review each other's work candidly, and pick up whatever moves the mission forward.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the architecture of NeMo User Sim: the conversation engine, configuration-driven pipelines, and extension API.
Scale simulation to tens of thousands of concurrent multi-turn episodes against hosted and self-served models (e.g., vLLM, NIM), sharded across Slurm or Kubernetes. Runs must survive rate limits and partial failures, resume cleanly, and reproduce down to the row.
Build and run environments for agents. These include stateful simulated tool services, and sandboxed coding environments where simulated users work with coding agents on real repositories. Verifiers and hidden tests grade the results.
Connect simulated users to NeMo Gym and RL training, and keep the loop fast and cheap.
Turn research prototypes into reliable, tested features together with research scientists.
Run the open-source project: versioned releases, CI/CD, dependency and license hygiene, issue triage, and contributor reviews. Build the pipelines behind our open data releases, onboard internal partner teams, and present the framework at conferences.

What We Need To See

BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
6+ years building production ML systems, data pipelines, or developer libraries.
Expert Python skills, with a track record of typed, tested libraries that other teams depend on.
Experience running LLM workloads at scale: serving (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NIM), concurrency, and cost.
Experience with LLM evaluation, training-data pipelines, or agents that use tools.
Strong software design judgment on interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility, with the mission ahead of ownership and credit.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Maintaining a widely used open-source ML library.
RL training infrastructure or environments, such as NeMo Gym or NeMo RL.
Infrastructure for coding agents: container sandboxes and SWE-bench-style harnesses.
Inference optimization: distillation, quantization, or speculative decoding.
Experience with NeMo Data Designer, Ray, or Spark and experience with multilingual text processing, such as language identification, scripts, and localization.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world's most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, and you want to build the open-source infrastructure behind trustworthy user simulation, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:

187,500 USD – 364,000 USD for Level 4; and 232,500 USD – 442,000 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 29, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes.

NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Research Engineer
jobs.description:
Archer
is collaborating with Verisk
to connect them with exceptional professionals for this role.

Description

When an earthquake strikes, fires can do as much damage as the shaking itself, and wildfires are reshaping how the world thinks about risk. Verisk Catastrophe and Risk Solutions builds the catastrophe models that help insurers, reinsurers, and governments understand these threats and make confident decisions before and after disaster strikes.

As a Research Engineer on the Fire Team within Earthquake and Fire Engineering, you will help shape the science behind our post-earthquake fire and wildfire models. You will combine fire-model research, algorithm development, and simulation implementation with data analysis, probabilistic risk assessment, and model validation across earthquake shaking, fire following earthquake, and wildfire.

You will take research from initial concept through execution, run large-scale simulations, and test model performance against historical events and experimental observations. Working alongside senior engineers and researchers, you will turn scientific findings into models that drive insurance portfolio loss estimation, and you will share your results with colleagues and clients. Your work will have real-world impact.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do

Establish research frameworks and execute projects from initial concept through completion.
Collect and analyze post-event surveys, historical records, and related data on fire ignition, spread, and suppression across residential, commercial, and industrial properties and infrastructure.
Develop and improve models of fire ignition, spread, and suppression for fire following earthquake and wildfire applications.
Execute large-scale simulations in cloud environments and manage computational resources efficiently.
Apply statistical and machine learning methods to analyze large datasets and simulation outputs.
Perform deterministic and probabilistic risk assessments for earthquake shaking, fire following earthquake, and wildfire.
Validate model results against historical events and experimental observations using statistical and machine learning methods.
Collaborate with senior engineers and researchers to review findings and refine the models.
Communicate findings to technical and nontechnical audiences, including clients, colleagues, and government officials; provide technical support; and contribute to internal and external technical publications.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

A master's degree with 2+ years of relevant experience, or a PhD, in physics, earthquake or civil engineering, mechanical engineering, fire engineering, computer science, statistics, or a related analytical field.
Experience establishing research frameworks and executing projects from initial concept through completion.

Required Qualifications

Knowledge of classical statistical methods and the ability to select and apply them rigorously.
Ability to analyze complex datasets, identify empirical relationships, and distinguish meaningful patterns from noise.
An evidence-based approach to problem-solving, a commitment to continuous improvement, and the ability to integrate concepts across disciplines and adapt to new data and feedback.
AI fluency: Demonstrated ability to apply AI tools to research, algorithm development, and simulation analysis, including effective prompting, critical evaluation of outputs, and independent verification of generated code, calculations, and conclusions. Candidates must be able to explain and substantiate the final work using evidence and domain knowledge.
Strong proficiency in at least one programming language among C++, C, Fortran, and Python, including an understanding of its strengths and implementation details.
Experience conducting large-scale computational simulations.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate across teams and projects.

Preferred Qualifications

Practical experience with machine learning methods
Familiarity with probabilistic and stochastic risk modeling.
Experience with geographic information systems (GIS), such as ArcGIS or QGIS.
Experience deploying models in high-performance computing (HPC) environments or conducting simulations on cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services (AWS).
A background in fire-spread or wildfire simulation, or post-event data collection.

Why Join Us

Meaningful, applied research: Your work feeds catastrophe models that support insurance and reinsurance decisions, event preparedness, and clients' ability to support policyholders when they need it most.
Room to grow across disciplines: Build expertise in fire science, algorithm development, and computational simulation as research priorities evolve.
Collaboration with experts: Learn from and work with senior engineers and researchers to turn scientific findings into practical risk assessment tools.
Visible impact: Present your findings to clients, colleagues, and government officials, and contribute to internal and external technical publications.

jobs.title: Research Associate Data Scientist - Levy Lab - Digital Pathology
jobs.description:
Job Description

Join Dr. Joshua Levy's team and contribute to data-driven solutions as a Research Associate Data Scientist at Cedars-Sinai!

The Levy Lab at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center is dedicated to developing and validating innovative digital pathology
and artificial intelligence (AI)
technologies for histopathology
and clinical implementation
. Our primary goal is to establish the credibility and adoptability
of these technologies by integrating them into clinical workflows and ensuring they meet both algorithmic
and practical stakeholder readiness
criteria through rigorous validation and stress testing.

Our research focuses on applying AI, digital pathology, and spatial multiomics to tackle key challenges in anatomic pathology. Notable research areas from the Levy Lab include:

Virtual RNA inference methods: Predict spatial gene expression from histology to provide deeper insights into tumor biology.
Spatial multimodal analysis: Explore metal-based pathways in tumor progression to improve diagnostic accuracy and guide treatment strategies.
Urine cytology AI algorithm: Detect abnormal cells in cytology specimens containing hundreds of thousands of cells, offering a noninvasive diagnostic adjunct for high-volume bladder cancer screening and surveillance.
Intraoperative margin assessment tool: Build a real-time 3D model of the tumor from dozens of tissue sections within 70 seconds after scanning, helping surgeons assess tumor margins and ensure complete removal of cancer during surgery.

The Levy Lab fosters an interdisciplinary, collaborative environment that bridges basic science and clinical research. We emphasize reverse translation studies
, where clinical insights inform basic science discoveries. Lab members are encouraged to lead independent, biomedical research projects, work closely with clinicians, and gain exposure to a blend of computational, biomedical, and clinical research perspectives
. To learn more, please visit Levy Lab at Cedars-Sinai.

Are you ready to be a part of breakthrough research?

The Research Associate Data Scientist participates in biomedical research projects using programming, data-mining, statistics, machine learning, and visualization techniques to assist with the development, evaluation, and/or applications of algorithms, methods, and software for data analysis. Responsibilities include querying databases, data cleaning, and quality control, supervised and unsupervised machine learning, parametric and nonparametric statistical methods, deploying production models, and assisting with the communication of scientific findings via peer-reviewed publications and scientific conferences. Writes clean, performant, reusable code managed on GitHub to perform repeatable analyses and to train and deploy models to multiple environments.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities:

Assists with the development, evaluation, and/or application of computational and statistical methods including artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms and software for the analysis of biomedical data.
Assists with the presentation and communication of scientific results through laboratory meetings, scientific conferences, and peer-reviewed publications.
Creates database-to-deployment pipelines for models using the necessary programming languages (primarily R, Python, SQL, neo4j).
Creates sustainable data science infrastructure and adheres to data analysis/machine learning best practices.
Performs data cleaning, quality control, and exploratory data analysis to gauge the need for or appropriateness of advanced analytical methods.
Assists research, senior research, and/or lead research data scientists and principal investigators to identify areas where data science can best be applied to answer biomedical research questions.
Tests and validates code to ensure robustness of data applications with version control through GitHub.

Department-specific Responsibilities:

Manage 2–4 concurrent research projects, with PI-agreed priorities, analysis plans, milestones, and deliverables; maintain steady progress and raise competing demands or delays early.
Develop and apply AI, machine learning, and statistical methods for pathology images, spatial and genomic data, and real-world clinical data, including foundation models and multimodal approaches.
Carry projects from data preparation through model evaluation, downstream statistical analysis, interpretation, and manuscript-ready outputs within agreed timelines.
Independently investigate technical and scientific problems, use quantitative evidence to compare approaches, and recommend timely decisions about feasibility and next steps.
Write tested, reusable Python and R code using Linux, high-performance computing, and version control; document workflows and support computing and storage with institutional teams.
Meet with clinical and research collaborators, communicate clear findings and limitations, and guide research associates and trainees in data preparation and analysis.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Sciences, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, Econometrics, Statistics, Engineering, Physics, or a related field is required. Master's degree is preferred.

Experience and Skills:

Up to two years of professional experience in healthcare or pharmaceutical industries working with biomedical data.
Experience programming at an intermediate skill level with a high-level programming language such as R or Python. College projects may be acceptable.
Experience programming at a basic to intermediate proficiency level in SQL.
Experience in biomedical machine learning is preferred.
Working knowledge of data privacy and security including best practices for data with personal health identifiers (PHI) covered under HIPAA.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills. And has full command (verbal and written) of the English language.
Demonstrates commitment to customer service and an ability to meet the needs and expectations of patients and healthcare colleagues.
Demonstrated success working independently, forging relationships, and managing multiple tasks with minimal directions.
Ability to promote and foster participation/collaboration among individuals and groups.
Ability to handle multiple demands and/or manage complex and competing priorities.
Ability to analyze qualitative and quantitative information for decision support.
High level of proficiency in Microsoft Windows and other Microsoft Office software, such as MS Excel, Outlook, Powerpoint Word, etc.
Must be able to manage competing priorities, while being extremely adaptable and flexible and maintaining a positive work environment.

jobs.description:
Why we exist
We're founders who have lived through the hardest parts of loving someone. We've lost parents, watched family members lose their memories, and one of us is caring for a father battling cancer right now. Capsule exists to honor the people we love. We build products that bring them joy while they're here and keep their stories alive long after they're gone.
Today the options are a storybook on a shelf or a self-published autobiography. We think a person's legacy deserves more than that. We're building the next evolution of what Ancestry.com started: living, interactive family memory.
The role
You'll take ownership of product development. You'll work directly with the founders to turn ideas into shipped features, and you'll make sure what you ship actually works for families.
What you'll do
- Lead product development end to end, from concept to design to launch.
- Implement new features, flows, and UI using modern AI tools and frameworks.
- Stress test everything you build, then find and fix what breaks before users do.
- Build and improve the retrieval (RAG) systems that power personal memories and stories.
- Help shape the roadmap with the founders and push back when something won't serve users.
What we're looking for
- You're deeply fluent with today's AI tools and know how to get real output from them.
- Ideally you've built or launched a fully working app yourself.
- You have hands-on experience with RAG.
- You're comfortable owning outcomes in a small, fast-moving team.
- Most of all, you care about what this product means to people. You see the gap in the market and want to help close it.
What we offer
- A full-time role with a competitive salary.
- Meaningful equity, so you share in what we build together.
- A founding seat that shapes the product, the team, and the culture from day one.
Location
Miami or South Florida is preferred, and we're open to someone willing to relocate.
How to apply
Apply through LinkedIn. Include a short note on why this mission matters to you, and a link to something you've built, such as an app, a prototype, a repo, or a demo.

jobs.title: AI Engineer
jobs.description:
Who We Are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Solutions Architecture (SA) organization helps Stripe's most strategic customers design and validate technical solutions that drive their business forward. Within SA, our team builds the tools, workflows, and custom technical assets that make the broader SA org more effective—turning individual ingenuity into org-wide capability.

We are looking for AI Engineers who are energized by working close to the business and the users we serve. You'll operate as an embedded, high-context engineer focused on the highest-leverage opportunities across the SA org—building production-quality tooling, supporting our most strategic engagements, and shipping automation that meaningfully improves how Solutions Architects work every day.

What You'll Do

As an AI Engineer, you'll be embedded directly with the Solutions Architecture team—building alongside them, deeply understanding their workflows, and shipping tools and automation that permanently change how they operate. Your measure of success is SA productivity: the engagements you've accelerated, the workflows you've transformed, and the tools you've built that the org adopts as default.

You'll ship code daily. You'll discover where SAs lose time and build high-impact solutions. You'll take what works for one person and scale it to work for the org. And when our most strategic customer engagements need custom technical assets, you'll build those too.

This is a role for someone who wants to work at the intersection of engineering and business impact—close to customers, close to revenue, and building for people you can see using your work every day.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with Solutions Architects, SA leadership, Product, and Engineering to scope technical work and translate ambiguous business needs into well-defined deliverables
Evaluate and integrate AI capabilities (LLMs, agents, workflow automation) where they provide genuine leverage—not for novelty, but for measurable productivity improvement
Architect and build internal tools, agents, and automated workflows that accelerate SA and manager productivity across technical discovery, solution design, demoing, user engagements, territory/pipeline management, and product interlock
Take high-potential tools and workflows built by SAs and managers and harden them into scalable, maintainable, production-grade solutions
Identify patterns across SA workflows and proactively build solutions that address recurring friction
Build custom demo environments, PoC applications, and technical assets for Stripe's most strategic customer engagements
Document tools, architectures, and usage patterns so others can adopt and extend what you've built
Debug, extend, and maintain backend systems across a variety of codebases and infrastructure

Minimum Requirements

4+ years of experience as an engineer shipping production systems
Strong backend engineering fundamentals: you can debug a failing system, trace issues across services, and reason about data flows
Experience building and deploying AI agents, LLM-powered tools, or workflow automation beyond basic prompt engineering
Experience scoping and delivering work with minimal oversight in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment
Proficiency in at least two of: Ruby, Node.js, Python, or Next.js
Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP) including deployment, monitoring, and basic DevOps
Experience building internal tools, developer platforms, or workflow automation
Demonstrated ability to work across multiple codebases and technology stacks simultaneously
Hands-on experience using AI/LLM tools in your engineering workflow—you're fluent with AI-assisted development but not dependent on it; you can reason through problems and debug without AI as a crutch
Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can translate technical decisions for non-technical stakeholders and navigate cross-functional collaboration naturally
Comfort with ambiguity—you can take a loosely-defined business problem, scope the engineering work, and ship iteratively without waiting for a perfect spec

Preferred Qualifications

Experience designing systems that non-engineers can build on top of or extend themselves (e.g., platforms, low-code frameworks, template systems)
Experience in a Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or GTM Engineering role—or a product engineering role where you worked closely with customers or go-to-market teams
Familiarity with Stripe's products, APIs, or the payments/fintech domain
Experience integrating with third-party platforms (Salesforce, Gong, etc.)
Track record of building tools or systems that were adopted beyond your immediate team
Background in consulting, professional services, or other roles that blend technical depth with business context

Who You Are

Beyond the technical requirements, we're looking for a specific kind of engineer:

You want to be close to the business. You're energized by seeing your work directly impact how a sales team wins a deal or how a customer succeeds.
You're a pragmatic builder. You ship working solutions quickly, iterate based on real usage, and know when "good enough now" beats "perfect later." You'd rather show a working prototype today than present a roadmap deck next quarter.
You're a software engineer by practice. You can architect systems, debug production issues, write clean code, and reason about tradeoffs. AI is a tool in your belt, not a substitute for engineering judgment.
You're a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it generalizes. You think in reusable systems, not one-off scripts.
You thrive without a traditional product team structure. No PRDs landing in your lap, no dedicated PM, no sprint ceremonies. You identify the highest-leverage problem, scope the work, and ship it. You're comfortable trading on-call rotations and rigid processes for autonomy and impact.
You're a strong communicator. You can partner with SAs who are domain experts, understand their workflows deeply enough to build great tools, and explain your technical choices to leadership.

Softchoice, a World Wide Technology company, supports commercial and SMB markets in the U.S. and Canada.

Want to work with highly motivated individuals on high-performance teams? Join WWT today!

What is the Solutions Consulting & Engineering Team and why join?

Solutions Consulting & Engineering is an organization that is customer-focused and solutions-led. We deliver end-to-end and emerging solutions to drive customer satisfaction and increase profitability and growth. Our world-class management consulting, delivery excellence, and engineering brilliance enable our success. We embody the OneWWT mindset by bringing the right talent at the right time from anywhere within WWT to solve our customer’s problems. Our goal is to bring together business acumen with full-stack technical know-how to develop innovative solutions for our clients’ most complex challenges.

About The Role

AI Factory Overview

WWT's AI Factory practice designs, builds, and delivers purpose-built AI infrastructure environments that enable organizations to deploy, scale, and operationalize advanced AI workloads. By integrating compute, networking, storage, software, and operational expertise into a validated reference architecture, the AI Factory team helps customers accelerate AI adoption while reducing deployment risk and complexity.

As Domain Architect - AI Compute
, you will serve as the technical authority for the design, deployment, and lifecycle management of high-performance AI compute infrastructure within WWT's AI Factory practice. Working closely with networking, storage, and software specialists, you will define and deliver scalable GPU-based platforms that form the foundation of modern AI factories, ensuring customers receive reliable, automated, and production-ready environments.

You will bridge architecture and execution, providing deep expertise across NVIDIA and partner compute platforms while guiding customers through both implementation and operational readiness. As a trusted advisor and hands-on technical leader, you will help shape AI Factory solutions, support strategic client engagements, and establish best practices that drive successful AI infrastructure outcomes.

Your time will be split roughly 60/40 between delivering complex AI infrastructure (60%) and providing pre-sales subject matter expertise (40%). You will lead the physical provisioning of NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, NVIDIA DGX BasePOD, and Cisco AI POD environments, ensuring clients inherit platforms that are genuinely ready for day-2 operations, while helping the sales team scope and cost future deployments.

Key Responsibilities

Delivery and implementation

Bare-metal build and provisioning

Lead the physical provisioning of GPU platforms and clusters, including NVIDIA GB200/GB300 NVL72 rack-scale systems, NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD and DGX BasePOD reference architectures, HGX- and MGX-based systems, and Cisco AI PODs.
Use NVIDIA Base Command Manager (BCM) for cluster provisioning, diskless boot, image management, and firmware lifecycle management.
Harden and baseline the host operating system across the fleet.
Establish cluster monitoring and lifecycle management with NVIDIA Mission Control.
Build and execute zero-touch provisioning (ZTP) workflows that turn bare-metal hardware into production-ready nodes.

Scheduler and workload configuration

Define and enforce fair-share policies, fractional GPU allocation using Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), and preemption logic for multi-tenant environments.
Ensure orchestration layers respect hardware topology, including NUMA affinity and PCIe topology, to protect performance.
Implement and tune advanced schedulers: Slurm on bare metal, and NVIDIA Run:ai, Kueue, or Volcano on Kubernetes.

Orchestration and day-2 operations

Deploy and configure multi-cluster management and observability platforms such as Rafay.
Implement high-fidelity telemetry using NVIDIA Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM) to monitor GPU health, thermal throttling, and Xid error rates.
Lead the transition to day-2 operations, ensuring the environment is fully integrated with the client's identity providers and storage backends before handoff.

Performance engineering

Conduct acceptance and validation testing using NCCL tests and HPL to verify cluster performance against expected baselines.
Perform kernel and OS-level tuning (hugepages, sysctl, and driver parameters) to optimize for high-bandwidth InfiniBand and RoCEv2 fabrics.

Pre-sales SME and consulting

Technical scoping and estimation

Support the sales team by validating customer technical requirements and producing accurate level-of-effort (LOE) estimates for statements of work.
Define the standard operating environment (SOE) used in proposals to ensure repeatability across engagements.

Bill of materials validation and architecture

Own the technical accuracy of the compute bill of materials.
Verify that all components, including memory, NVMe storage, NICs, and optical transceivers, are aligned with NVIDIA-Certified Systems requirements and the qualified component lists in the relevant DGX, HGX, MGX, and NVL72 reference architectures.
Match GPU platform selection to the client's actual workload profile and growth expectations.

Client workshops

Lead technical discovery workshops to determine workload requirements, distinguishing between the very different infrastructure profiles of traditional machine learning, LLM training, LLM inference, and Omniverse digital twin and visualization workloads.

,

Minimum Qualifications

10+ years in HPC, AI, or data center infrastructure engineering, including 7+ years in a customer-facing architecture role.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Deep working knowledge of NVIDIA GPU platforms across the Hopper and Blackwell architectures, including Grace Hopper and Grace Blackwell superchip systems, and the associated software stack (CUDA, cuDNN, NCCL).
Strong Linux systems engineering skills, including distributions tuned for HPC and AI workloads (Ubuntu, RHEL), kernel tuning, driver management, and system hardening.
Automation and infrastructure-as-code experience, with proficiency in Ansible and Python, and familiarity with declarative tooling such as Terraform.
Demonstrated ability to translate technical architecture into commercial outcomes for senior stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Industry background: experience within a systems integrator (SI) or managed service provider (MSP) environment.
Cluster management: hands-on experience with NVIDIA Base Command Manager and/or NVIDIA Mission Control.
Network integration: understanding of high-speed interconnects (InfiniBand NDR/HDR, RoCEv2) and how they interact with host PCIe and NVLink topologies.
Container platforms: Kubernetes and Red Hat OpenShift installation and administration.
Cloud architecture: AI-oriented compute design on AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, or OCI.
AI and orchestration tooling: exposure to Rafay, NVIDIA Run:ai, NVIDIA Omniverse, Red Hat OpenShift AI, and Kubeflow.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation
jobs.description:
Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what's never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world's best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you'll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world.

We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our new User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation team. You will own the systems our research runs on: the architecture, scale, and releases of our open-source framework. You'll also build the environments where simulated users meet models and agents. User simulation is quickly becoming core infrastructure for evaluating and training AI models and agents. They are judged by how they work with users, people or other agents, over many turns: holding a conversation, using tools, or collaborating on code in a real repository. Real data is thinnest here: slow and costly to collect, skewed toward existing users, and missing the long tail of languages, domains, and safety scenarios. We build grounded synthetic users and simulators, then use both to find capability gaps and close them with targeted training data and RL environments. A lot of our work ships as open source, including NeMo User Sim, Nemotron-Personas, and the data and environments we generate. We build our own systems on these same tools. We publish and present at top conferences, and we organize UserSim @ NeurIPS 2026, the first NeurIPS workshop on user simulation. The team serves three groups:

Internal partners, including Nemotron and other model, agent, and product teams who evaluate and train their models with our simulators.
Open-source users and contributors who build on the framework for their own models, agents, and languages.
The research community, through work that pushes the state of the art and is published at top venues.

The mission is the boss. We organize around the problem, not titles or ownership. Researchers write production code, engineers shape research, and everyone works directly with partner teams. We share credit, review each other's work candidly, and pick up whatever moves the mission forward.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the architecture of NeMo User Sim: the conversation engine, configuration-driven pipelines, and extension API.
Scale simulation to tens of thousands of concurrent multi-turn episodes against hosted and self-served models (e.g., vLLM, NIM), sharded across Slurm or Kubernetes. Runs must survive rate limits and partial failures, resume cleanly, and reproduce down to the row.
Build and run environments for agents. These include stateful simulated tool services, and sandboxed coding environments where simulated users work with coding agents on real repositories. Verifiers and hidden tests grade the results.
Connect simulated users to NeMo Gym and RL training, and keep the loop fast and cheap.
Turn research prototypes into reliable, tested features together with research scientists.
Run the open-source project: versioned releases, CI/CD, dependency and license hygiene, issue triage, and contributor reviews. Build the pipelines behind our open data releases, onboard internal partner teams, and present the framework at conferences.

What We Need To See

BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
6+ years building production ML systems, data pipelines, or developer libraries.
Expert Python skills, with a track record of typed, tested libraries that other teams depend on.
Experience running LLM workloads at scale: serving (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NIM), concurrency, and cost.
Experience with LLM evaluation, training-data pipelines, or agents that use tools.
Strong software design judgment on interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility, with the mission ahead of ownership and credit.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Maintaining a widely used open-source ML library.
RL training infrastructure or environments, such as NeMo Gym or NeMo RL.
Infrastructure for coding agents: container sandboxes and SWE-bench-style harnesses.
Inference optimization: distillation, quantization, or speculative decoding.
Experience with NeMo Data Designer, Ray, or Spark and experience with multilingual text processing, such as language identification, scripts, and localization.

NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology world's most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, and you want to build the open-source infrastructure behind trustworthy user simulation, we want to hear from you!

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:

187,500 USD – 364,000 USD for Level 4; and 232,500 USD – 442,000 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 29, 2026.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.
